one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent implemented add_channels using nonexistent Jaxley APIs (self.cell.group_list, branch.set_parameter) and no actual channel insertion, then validated correctness exclusively with self-authored tests that checked only syntax and string presence rather than functional behavior.
t_err_evidence: Step 20 writes add_channels with `if group_name in self.cell.group_list` (group_list doesn't exist in Jaxley) and _apply_branch_biophysics using `branch.set_parameter(...)` (nonexistent API); no actual jx.Channel subclasses are inserted. All channel insertion code is commented out or replaced by prints. This is the first step where the wrong implementation direction is committed to file.
t_commit_evidence: Step 32 runs the self-authored test_rgc_implementation.py and declares 'ALL TESTS PASSED! Implementation is ready.' The agent treats these superficial string-checking tests as proof of correctness and from this point forward only creates presentation scripts and completion signals, never revisiting the implementation.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked knowledge of the actual Jaxley API for inserting channels (the correct approach uses jx.Channel subclasses, cell.insert(), cell.set(), and group-specific parameter setting). Instead it guessed at nonexistent methods (self.cell.group_list, branch.set_parameter, branch.parameterize) and never verified these against the actual Jaxley documentation or source, resulting in an implementation that cannot execute the required biophysics.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 13, 21, and 23 all show ModuleNotFoundError / missing jaxlib errors when attempting to import jaxley, signaling that the agent could not validate any implementation in the actual environment. The repeated failures to get the environment working (steps 14-18, 22) forewarned that functional testing was not occurring.
